findings.claim: TOP RECOMMENDATION. Make the smoke run a re-runnable recorded command, and give the re-compare a concrete command. FR-007/T001 prove the recipe once, on one host version, by one person. With no maintainer capacity nobody re-runs it, so the verified-on claim rots silently. FR-003's 're-compare after a plugin update' is a memory step with no command. Remedy: T001 writes research.md as a copy-paste block (cp, edit, a dispatch prompt asking the reviewer to state its model/effort, expected output). Add a README diff command against the shipped file ignoring frontmatter, and a dated 'verified on host version X' line.

evidence.note: FR-007 requires one run recorded with host version, not a re-runnable block.
T001 records the steps 'as run' and says nothing of re-running them.

findings.pull_quote: A check only one person ran once is a story, not a gate.

findings.claim: A per-project install lands in the same directory as the retune copies, and --force overwrites them silently. Spec.md:57 says the installer writes only under the Claude home, but install.sh documents CLAUDE_HOME=$PWD/.claude as the per-project install, so its target is the project's .claude/agents/ where the copy sits. Without --force the copy is kept; with it, replaced with no warning, losing the retune and its reason comment. Remedy: one README sentence, never pass --force over a retuned reviewer in a project install; no code change, so FR-001 holds.

evidence.note: --force copies over any existing destination file.
Only a pre-existing global customization is tested, not a per-project copy.
The spec treats the installer as writing only under the Claude home.

findings.pull_quote: The one flag that overwrites the copy lives in the same directory the copy lives in.

findings.claim: The 3am reader cannot see that a copy was in play, and the recipe gives no rollback. The record omission is settled and I do not re-argue it, but the file route is open: listing the project's .claude/agents/ shows which reviewers are overridden, and deleting the copy restores the shipped agent. FR-003 names neither. Remedy: two README sentences, how to see overrides and how to roll back, and a reason comment carrying the date and the shipped version copied from.

evidence.note: The review record does not show that a reviewer ran from a copy.
FR-003 lists recipe steps but no check or rollback.

findings.pull_quote: If the record cannot say a copy ran, the README must at least say where to look and how to undo it.

findings.claim: Staleness has no signal. The accepted cost is a forked persona the installer never refreshes, and a global-install copy sits outside the manifest, so it cannot be reported. The retuner feels it later, with a reviewer whose gates predate the canon. Remedy: require the reason comment to record the plugin version or commit copied from, so the diff target is known (pairs with F31). No tooling.

evidence.note: Keeping a copy current is out of scope with no staleness check.
The manifest covers only files the installer wrote.

findings.pull_quote: A copy that does not say what it was copied from cannot be compared with anything.

findings.claim: Host-version claims in the README will age with no owner. Accept the rot but make it legible: a dated verified-on line, and keep every behaviour claim a link to host docs, as SC-004 already requires.

evidence.note: The recipe names the host version the smoke ran on, and effort depends on it.

findings.pull_quote: Unowned docs rot; dating them lets the reader discount them.

findings.claim: Complexity is earned: docs-only is the right size with no maintainer capacity. No code, no CI change, no new failure mode; T005 reuses the existing integrity gate. Nothing boring is missing beyond the README sentences in F31 to F34. I deliberately do not prescribe a staleness checker, a record field or a CI test of host resolution.

evidence.note: The existing integrity gate runs on push and PR and is reused unchanged.
FR-001 keeps chorus from reading, applying or validating any run setting.

findings.pull_quote: The cheapest operability is the code you did not ship.
